paper.title: On the Regularity and Fairness of Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit with fairness constraints and reward regularity
unmapped: Per-arm minimum average reward requirements lambda_n are known to the learner and assumed feasible with slack delta > 0
Regularity objective: running average of Time-Since-Last-Reward (age-of-information-like) metrics
Learner needs epsilon <= delta/2 (knowledge of a lower bound on the feasibility slack delta)
Regret is measured against the optimal randomized stationary policy satisfying the fairness constraints with slack delta
settings.definition_quote: We consider a combinatorial multi-armed bandit with $N$ arms, where multiple arms can be pulled simultaneously in each round. ... $\{X_n(t)\}_{t\geq0}$ are independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Bernoulli random variables with unknown mean $\mu_n\in(0,1]$ ... the fairness means that each arm $n$ is at least received the reward $\lambda_n>0$ on average

conditions: fairness requirements feasible with slack delta > 0
K denotes the paper's N (number of arms); m denotes S_max (max arms pulled per round)

source.label: prop:regret
source.quote: [Cumulative Regret] Under the RFL algorithm with $\epsilon\leq\delta$, the cumulative regret $\text{Reg}(T)$ over consecutive $T$ rounds can be bounded from above as follows: \text{Reg}(T)\leq \min \{S_{\max}\mu_{\max}T, \frac{NT}{\mu_{\min}} (\frac{\alpha + 1}{\beta }) +2\sqrt{6NS_{\max}T\log T} +N(1+\frac{5\pi^2}{12}) \}.

results.notes: Regret is defined via means against the optimal fair randomized stationary policy q*, so pseudo-regret vs best feasible policy. Table 1 instantiations: alpha=0, beta=O(sqrt T) gives O(sqrt(T log T)); alpha=O(T^{1/6}), beta=O(sqrt T) gives O(T^{2/3}).

symbols.eps_alg: virtual-queue slack parameter epsilon of RFL

conditions: fairness requirements feasible with slack delta > 0

source.label: prop:zero_violation
source.quote: [Zero Cumulative Fairness Violations] Under the RFL algorithm, if $\epsilon \leq \delta/2$, there exists a zero violation point $t_0\triangleq g_0(\alpha,\beta)/\epsilon=O((\alpha^2\log\alpha+\beta)/\epsilon)$ after which the zero cumulative fairness violation is achieved for any round $t\geq t_0$

results.notes: Bound on the zero-violation round t0 after which cumulative expected fairness violation is exactly zero; explicit g_0 depends on N, lambda_min, mu_min, delta.

symbols.g_0: constant g_0(alpha,beta)=O(alpha^2 log alpha + beta) defined in Proposition on zero violation

conditions: fairness requirements feasible with slack delta > 0

source.label: prop:age
source.quote: [Short-term Reward Regularity] Under the RFL algorithm, if $\epsilon\leq\delta/2$, then the running average of total expected TSLR metrics over consecutive $T$ rounds can be bounded as follows: \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\bE[Z_n(t)] \leq \min\{\frac{N+g_0(\alpha,\beta)}{\lambda_{\min}}, \frac{N^2}{\delta\mu_{\min}} ( 1 + \frac{3\beta+4}{\alpha} )\}.

results.notes: Bound on running average of expected TSLR (regularity metric), not regret; kept as average (not multiplied by T) since it is not a regret quantity.
